A01.text: Maya, look! A 2003 Accord... forty-eight hundred bucks. The seller says it runs great.

A02.text: Oh, nice! Have you seen it in person?

A03.text: Not yet. He's out of state, so he wants a five hundred dollar deposit to hold it.

A04.text: He's in the navy. On a submarine. But apparently, the Wi-Fi down there is amazing.

B01.text: That is exactly how my cousin lost his money.

C01.text: And even when the car is real, one strip of tape can hide a check-engine light.

D01.text: TireKick. The car proves itself, before anyone haggles.

E01.text: The seller gets a one-time code, and films one continuous take. The code, next to the VIN. Every warning light at key-on. Then, the engine start.

F01.text: Meta's Muse Spark watches the video, and reports what it sees. Our code makes the call. The model never decides the verdict.

G01.text: This seller's video had no code, a VIN that fails the check digit, and a deposit request.

H01.text: Wow. Glad I didn't send that five hundred.

H02.text: You almost sent five hundred bucks to a submarine.

I01.text: An honest seller passes, with one flag: an airbag recall on this model. TireKick turns that into leverage.

J01.text: Every price comes from code. Never above your max. Every ask cites real evidence, and you approve each message.

K01.text: Forty-four hundred! That's four hundred under asking.

P01.text: Find the car on Facebook Marketplace. TireKick checks it, right inside WhatsApp.

S01.text: In our tests, TireKick caught all six spoof attempts. And it got eighty-four percent of the possible discount. A student on their own got fifty-one.

Z01.text: Meta's Muse finds the car, and haggles. TireKick makes the car prove itself.
